summary: The two-attempt filter drops every path an earlier attempt reported from changedPaths, even when the accepted last attempt also reports it. summary: Repeat passes now emit the "single final" Scope Check again, and fix-range passes emit it with a false or partial `Diff read`. Where: review/SKILL.md.tmpl Step 3 item 5 (rendered as review/SKILL.md:266, "5. Now emit Step 1.5's final Scope Check; `Diff read` records this read."), together with Step 5.8 §1 ("Below 3, repeat Steps 3–5 ... On a repeat, execute Steps 3–5 in order"). Failure: item 5 has no condition. After an edited pass, Step 5.8 starts the next pass with `--start review --fix-range`, and Step 3 then diffs against FIX_BASE, which reads only the fix range. Item 5 runs again on that pass, so the reviewer emits a second "single final" Scope Check with one of two outcomes. If it reports honestly, `Diff read: partial (...)`, the rule in plan-completion/sideways turns that into `DRIFT DETECTED` naming every unread path. That is a false drift verdict, and it overrides the first pass's CLEAN in the final report. If it doesn't, it writes `Diff read: full` for a read that wasn't full, and that recorded field is exactly what decides whether CLEAN and options B/C count as approved. Up to 3 cycles plus the final full pass can produce up to 4 conflicting Scope Checks in one invocation. Before this change, the Scope Check was emitted once, at Step 1.5, which never repeats. Fix: limit item 5 to the invocation's first full pass, for example "5. On the invocation's first full pass only, emit Step 1.5's final Scope Check; `Diff read` records this read. Re-reviews never re-emit it." Add a test to review-workflow-clarity or sideways-review that asserts the condition.

summary: Retry validation loses ownership of documents edited by both attempts (`test/skill-e2e-ship-docsync.test.ts:92–100`). The new `retained` filter removes every path reported by an earlier attempt from the final changed-path set, even when the accepted attempt edits that same document again. A normal repair—attempt 1 updates the reference incorrectly, then attempt 2 corrects it and truthfully reports `updated` with the same `files_updated` path—therefore passes an empty `changedPaths` array to `vetDocsCompletion`, which throws `unreported edits`. I reproduced this using the actual validator with two successive `updated` contracts for one document. This makes the paid ship gate reject a valid repair within its newly supported two-attempt budget. The converse also loses coverage: after attempt 1 lists a path, attempt 2 can modify that path while claiming `current`, and this contract check cannot detect the unreported second edit. Aggregate write observation does not establish which attempt reported each edit. Compare each attempt against its own before/after snapshot or attribute native writes to their owning dispatch; do not subtract whole paths merely because an earlier attempt named them. Add regressions for both attempts editing the same path and for an unreported second edit.

The retained-edit filter takes out every path an earlier attempt reported, even when the accepted attempt reports the same path. Take a two-attempt run where attempt 1 updates DOC_PATH, the parent rejects it, and the repair attempt edits DOC_PATH again and reports status 'updated' with files_updated [DOC_PATH]. Here retained=[DOC_PATH], so changedPaths becomes [] and vetDocsCompletion (docsync-contract.ts:53) throws 'unreported edits'. A correct run goes red. The free replay test only covers the updated→current case and copies the filter formula instead of running runShipDocs, so this path has no coverage.
fix: Subtract retained paths only when the accepted contract does not claim them: changed.filter(p => contract.files_updated.includes(p) || !retained.includes(p)). Add an updated→updated case to the free two-attempt test.
evidence: docsync-contract.ts:53 compares sorted changedPaths with result.files_updated exactly; an 'updated' contract must have non-empty files_updated (line 35).

summary: [FIXABLE, medium] Every pass emits the "single final" Scope Check, including fix-range passes: review/SKILL.md.tmpl:98 (review/SKILL.md:266) Step 3 item 5 says "Now emit Step 1.5's final Scope Check; `Diff read` records this read" with no condition. Step 5.8 repeats Steps 3–5 after every edited pass, and item 2 of the same list starts those repeats with `--start review --fix-range`, which makes the pass diff against FIX_BASE. So an invocation with edits emits one Scope Check per pass, and the fix-range pass's check records a read that covers only the fix range. Under the rule at plan-completion.md:229 (sideways.ts:53), that read is `partial`, so the check is a spurious `DRIFT DETECTED` naming every path outside the fix range. The other possibility is that the agent writes `Diff read: full` for a fix-range read, which makes CLEAN, B and C look approved on a read that never covered the full diff. The final pass is always full, so the last check is correct, but nothing tells a consumer that the earlier "final" checks are superseded. A PR body or report that takes the first check it finds gets the wrong one. Fix: condition item 5, for example "On the first full pass only (never a `--fix-range` pass), emit…", or move it to the final zero-edit full pass in Step 5.8.

summary: A valid repair/re-audit of the same document is rejected by the release gate. `test/skill-e2e-ship-docsync.test.ts:93–99` subtracts every path reported by an earlier attempt from the aggregate changed-path list before validating the final attempt. A path is not owned exclusively by its first writer: attempt 1 can partially update a document, get rejected, and attempt 2 can correctly repair that same document and report it in `files_updated`. The subtraction then supplies `changedPaths: []` while the accepted contract reports that document, so `vetDocsCompletion` throws `unreported edits` and fails an otherwise valid ship-docsync-completion run. This is expressly permitted recovery: `ship/sections/documentation.md:122–126` requires a fresh snapshot of current inputs and validates the remaining attempt against that snapshot. Read-only reproduction using the actual validator: the second attempt with the document as its observed delta is accepted; applying the new aggregate-path filter to the same contracts throws `unreported edits`. Compare each attempt with its own pre-dispatch snapshot or observed write delta instead of inferring ownership by subtracting filenames. Add a regression where both attempts update the same document; the added replay covers only updated → current.
